ABS.doc: Returns the absolute value of a number.

ACS.doc: Returns the arc cosine (in radians) of a number between -1 and 1.

AND.doc: Bitwise AND. With two strings, returns a string whose bytes are the bitwise AND of the corresponding bytes; with two numbers, returns the numeric bitwise AND (e.g. AND(12,10)=8).

ARG.doc: Returns the n-th argument from the command line that started ProvideX; ARG(0) is the executable/program name. Errors if the argument does not exist.

ASC.doc: Returns the ASCII (byte) value of the first character of a string. Errors on a null string.

ASN.doc: Returns the arc sine (in radians) of a number between -1 and 1.

ATH.doc: ASCII-to-hex conversion: converts a string of hexadecimal digits into the corresponding binary string (ATH("41")="A"). Inverse of HTA().

ATN.doc: Returns the arc tangent (in radians) of a number.

BIN.doc: Converts an integer to a binary (two's complement, big-endian) string of the given length, e.g. BIN(65,2)=$0041$. See DEC() for the inverse.

params.name: length
params.doc: Length of the resulting string in bytes.

BSZ.doc: Returns memory block size information for the session (e.g. BSZ(0)). Exact meaning of the argument not confirmed.

CHG.doc: Internal/undocumented string function (returns a null string for ordinary text in 9.62).

CHR.doc: Returns the one-character string whose ASCII (byte) value is given, e.g. CHR(65)="A".

CMP.doc: Compresses a string (zlib-style); use UCP() to restore the original.

COS.doc: Returns the cosine of an angle given in radians.

CPL.doc: Compiles a ProvideX statement held in a string into its internal (tokenised) form; LST() converts it back to text.

CRC.doc: Returns a 2-byte CRC (cyclic redundancy check) of a string, optionally continuing from a previous 2-byte CRC seed.

params.name: seed$
params.doc: Optional 2-byte starting CRC (e.g. result of a previous CRC call).

CSE.doc: Internal function accepting a list of values of one type (all numeric or all string). Purpose not documented; returns 0 in tests.

CTL.doc: Returns control/terminal information for a channel and item. Exact semantics not confirmed.

CVS.doc: Convert string: applies the conversions selected by the (additive) code: 1 strip leading spaces, 2 strip trailing spaces, 4 upper-case, 8 lower-case, 16 replace non-printable characters with spaces, 32 compress multiple spaces to one, 256 capitalise words. E.g. CVS(A$,3) trims both ends.

DEC.doc: Converts a binary string to a signed (two's complement) integer, e.g. DEC($00FF$)=255, DEC($FF$)=-1. Inverse of BIN().

DIM.doc: Returns a string of the given length filled with spaces, or with repetitions of fill$ (truncated to length).

DIR.doc: Returns the current directory of a drive, e.g. DIR("") for the current drive, DIR("C:").

DLL.doc: Calls a function in a Windows DLL and returns its numeric result. Arguments after the function name are passed to the DLL function.

DLX.doc: Extended form of DLL(): calls a function in a Windows DLL (different calling/argument conventions).

DSK.doc: Returns the current disk drive (e.g. DSK("")="E:"), or validates/returns the given drive.

DTE.doc: Formats a Julian date (and optional time in hours) as a string. DTE(0) is today. Format codes include %Y year, %Yz 2-digit year, %M/%Mz month, %Ms/%Ml month name short/long, %D/%Dz day, %Ds/%Dl day name, %H/%Hz hour, %m/%mz minutes, %s seconds. Without a format the DAY_FORMAT style is used.

params.name: julian
params.doc: Julian date as returned by JUL() (0 = today).

params.name: time
params.doc: Optional time of day in hours (e.g. 12.5 = 12:30).

params.name: format$
params.doc: Optional format mask, after a colon.

ENV.doc: Returns the value of an operating-system environment variable, or with a number the n-th "NAME=value" entry of the environment. Returns "" if not set.

EPT.doc: Returns the decimal exponent of a number: the number of digits before the decimal point (e.g. EPT(1234.5)=4, EPT(0.05)=-1).

ERR.doc: Returns the position (1-based) of the current error number (ERR) within the argument list, or 0 if it is not in the list. Commonly used as ON ERR(11,12) GOTO ...

EVN.doc: Evaluates a numeric expression held in a string and returns its value, e.g. EVN("1+2")=3.

EVS.doc: Evaluates a string expression held in a string and returns its value.

EXP.doc: Returns 10 raised to the given power (EXP(1)=10). Note: ProvideX EXP/LOG use base 10.

FFN.doc: Find function: looks up a function/name and returns a reference number, or -1 if not found.

FIB.doc: Returns the File Information Block of an open channel: a binary string describing the file (type, key and record sizes, path, etc.).

FID.doc: Returns the file identifier/description string of an open channel (FID(0) is the terminal id).

FIN.doc: Returns file information for an open channel (binary string including counts, sizes, path). An optional item name selects specific information.

FPT.doc: Returns the fractional part of a number (FPT(12.75)=.75, FPT(-2.25)=-.25).

GAP.doc: Sets the high bit of each character to give odd parity (Generate ASCII Parity, odd). See GEP() for even parity.

GBL.doc: Reads or sets a global string value shared across programs: GBL(name$) returns it, GBL(name$, value$) sets and returns it.

GEP.doc: Adjusts the high bit of each character to give even parity. See GAP() for odd parity.

HSA.doc: Internal numeric function (returns 0 in tests); purpose not documented.

HSH.doc: Returns a hash of a string: with no type a 2-byte hash; type 1 = MD5, 2 = MD4, 3 = MD2, 4 = SHA-1 (binary results; use HTA() to display).

params.name: type
params.doc: Optional hash algorithm (1 MD5, 2 MD4, 3 MD2, 4 SHA-1).

HTA.doc: Hex-to-ASCII: returns the hexadecimal representation of a string (HTA("ABC")="414243"). Inverse of ATH().

HWN.doc: Returns the Windows handle (HWND) of the window associated with a channel (HWN(0) for the main window).

I3E.doc: IEEE conversion: with a number returns its 8-byte IEEE double representation; with an 8-byte string returns the number it encodes.

I86.doc: Intel-format numeric conversion function listed in the lexer table. It is not accepted by the 9.62 syntax checker in any tested argument form.

IND.doc: Returns the index (0-based relative record number) of the next record on the channel.

INT.doc: Returns the integer part of a number (truncates toward zero: INT(-2.5)=-2).

IOL.doc: Returns the IOList (embedded data dictionary IOList) associated with a channel, optionally a named one.

IOR.doc: Bitwise inclusive OR of two strings (byte by byte) or two integers (IOR(12,10)=14).

JST.doc: Justifies a string within the given length (truncating if longer). Mode 0 = right-justify, 1 = left-justify (default), 2 = centre; fill$ gives the pad character (default space).

JUL.doc: Returns the Julian day number for a date (relative to the 'BY' base-year parameter). JUL(year,month,day) or JUL(date$) where date$ is in the current DAY format. DTE() converts back.

KEC.doc: Returns the current key (key of the last record accessed) on the channel without reading the record.

KEF.doc: Returns the first key in the file (for the current or KNO= key chain) on the channel without reading the record.

KEL.doc: Returns the last key in the file (for the current or KNO= key chain) on the channel without reading the record.

KEN.doc: Returns the next key (key of the next record) on the channel without reading the record.

signatures.label: KEN(chan[, KNO=, IND=, KEY=, RNO=, END=ref, ERR=ref])

KEP.doc: Returns the prior key (key of the previous record) on the channel without reading the record.

signatures.label: KEP(chan[, KNO=, IND=, KEY=, RNO=, END=ref, ERR=ref])

KEY.doc: Returns the key of the next record on the channel without reading the record.

signatures.label: KEY(chan[, KNO=, IND=, RNO=, END=ref, ERR=ref])

KGN.doc: Key generation function: builds a key from a key definition and record data. Exact semantics not confirmed.

LCS.doc: Returns the string converted to lower case.

LEN.doc: Returns the length of a string in bytes.

LNO.doc: Returns the statement (line) number for a statement reference (e.g. a label or line number).

LOG.doc: Returns the base-10 logarithm of a positive number (LOG(100)=2).

LRC.doc: Returns a 1-byte longitudinal redundancy check (XOR of all bytes) of a string.

LST.doc: Converts a compiled (internal format) statement, e.g. from CPL() or PGM(), back into listable source text.

MAX.doc: Returns the largest of the numeric arguments.

MEM.doc: Memory access function: MEM(n) returns a number, MEM(n, length) returns a string. Exact semantics not confirmed.

MID.doc: Returns a substring starting at position start (1-based; negative counts from the end) for length characters (default: to the end).

MIN.doc: Returns the smallest of the numeric arguments.

MNM.doc: Returns the output sequence associated with a mnemonic for a channel.

MOD.doc: Returns the remainder of num divided by divisor (result has the sign of the divisor: MOD(-7,3)=2).

MSG.doc: Returns message text: MSG(n) gives the text for error number n; MSG(key$[, arg$...]) retrieves a message from the message library (MESSAGE_LIB).

MSK.doc: Searches a string using a regular-expression mask and returns the position of the first match (0 if none). The length of the match is placed in MSL.

MXC.doc: Returns the highest column number (0-based) of the window/terminal on the channel (e.g. 79).

MXL.doc: Returns the highest line number (0-based) of the window/terminal on the channel (e.g. 24).

NEW.doc: Creates a new object instance of the named class (DEF CLASS) and returns its object handle; extra arguments are passed to the ON_CREATE method.

NOT.doc: With a number, logical NOT (1 if zero, else 0). With a string, returns the bitwise complement of each byte.

NUL.doc: Returns 1 if the string is null or contains only spaces, otherwise 0.

NUM.doc: Converts a string to a number (commas are ignored); errors (#26) if the string is not numeric unless ERR= is given. VAL is an alias.

OBJ.doc: Returns binary information about a window/object on a channel. Exact semantics not confirmed.

OPT.doc: Returns the OPEN options (OPT= string) in effect for a channel.

PAD.doc: Pads or truncates a string to the given length. Mode 0 = pad on the left (right-justify), 1 = pad on the right (default), 2 = centre; fill$ gives the pad character.

PCK.doc: Packs a number into ProvideX packed (BCD-style) string format of the given length (default 8). UPK() unpacks it.

PFX.doc: Returns prefix (search path) information; PFX(0) returns the current prefix list (as in the PFX system variable).

PGM.doc: Returns program information: a compiled statement of the current program by number (see LST()), or PGM(-1) for the program name.

POS.doc: Returns the position in string$ where the relation with find$ is first satisfied (0 if none); usually POS(find$=string$). step gives the search increment (negative searches backwards from the end) and occurrence the n-th match (0 returns the count of matches).

params.name: find$=string$
params.doc: Relation: find$ followed by an operator (=, <>, <, >, <=, >=) and the string to search.

params.name: step
params.doc: Search step (default 1; negative searches from the end).

params.name: occurrence
params.doc: Which occurrence to find (0 = count occurrences).

PRC.doc: Rounds a number to the given number of decimal places (default: the current PRECISION).

PRM.doc: Returns the current value of a system parameter, e.g. PRM('BY'). The parameter is written as a quoted mnemonic like 'XX'.

PTH.doc: Returns the full path of the file/device open on a channel.

PUB.doc: Returns public (property/method) information for an object/channel. Exact semantics not confirmed.

RCD.doc: Returns the next (or the specified) record from the channel as a single string without moving into variables.

RDX.doc: Radix conversion of a string into a packed (radix-encoded) binary form.

REC.doc: Record function: builds/returns a record string from a composite string or IOList (honours SEP=).

REF.doc: Object reference function (e.g. reference count of an object handle).

RND.doc: Returns a random number: RND(0) gives a fraction between 0 and 1; a positive argument n returns an integer from 0 to n-1; a negative argument reseeds the generator. See also the RND system variable.

RNO.doc: Returns the record number of the next record on the channel.

signatures.label: RNO(chan[, KEY=k$][, KNO=n][, IND=n][, END=ref][, ERR=ref])

SCALL.doc: Alias of SYS(): executes an operating-system command and returns its exit status.

SEP.doc: Returns the field separator in effect for the given channel.

SGN.doc: Returns the sign of a number: -1, 0 or 1.

SIN.doc: Returns the sine of an angle given in radians.

SQR.doc: Returns the square root of a non-negative number.

SRT.doc: Sorts a string made of fixed-length segments of the given length into ascending order (SRT("ccbbaa",2)="aabbcc").

SSZ.doc: Returns a size value for the session (e.g. string/stack size). Exact semantics not confirmed.

STK.doc: Returns information about the program/GOSUB stack. Exact semantics not confirmed.

STP.doc: Strips characters (default spaces) from a string. Mode 0 = leading, 1 = trailing (default), 2 = both ends, 3 = all occurrences.

STR.doc: Converts a number to a string, optionally formatted with a mask after a colon (STR(1234.5:"#,##0.00")="1,234.50"). With a string argument, returns it unchanged.

SUB.doc: Substitutes new$ for every occurrence of old$ in string$, or only the given occurrence.

SWP.doc: Swaps byte order in a string: no mode reverses the string; 1 swaps adjacent byte pairs; 2 swaps 2-byte halves within each 4 bytes; 3 reverses each 4-byte group.

SYS.doc: Executes an operating-system command and returns its exit status. SCALL is an alias.

TAN.doc: Returns the tangent of an angle given in radians.

TBL.doc: Table lookup: TBL(index, v0, v1, ...) returns v0 when index is 0, v1 when 1, etc. (error if out of range). TBL(string$, from$, to$) translates characters of string$ found in from$ to the corresponding characters of to$.

params.name: value0
params.doc: Value returned for 0 (all values the same type).

TCB.doc: Task Control Block: TCB(n) returns numeric task/session information item n (e.g. current statement, error line, etc.). A string form TCB(name$) also exists.

TMR.doc: Timer function: returns elapsed time in seconds for a timer selector. Exact semantics not confirmed.

TRX.doc: Translation function on a string. Exact semantics not confirmed.

TSK.doc: Returns task/device configuration information for an entry number. Exact semantics not confirmed.

TXH.doc: Returns the height (in pixels) that text$ occupies in the current (or given) font.

TXW.doc: Returns the width (in pixels) that text$ occupies in the current (or given) font.

UCP.doc: Uncompresses a string produced by CMP().

UCS.doc: Returns the string converted to upper case.

UPK.doc: Unpacks a number stored in ProvideX packed format (see PCK()).

VAL.doc: Alias of NUM(): converts a string to a number.

VIN.doc: Returns the value of the numeric variable whose name is given in a string (VIN("X")); an object handle may precede the name to read an object property.

VIS.doc: Returns the value of the string variable whose name is given in a string (VIS("Y$")); an object handle may precede the name to read an object property.

XEQ.doc: Executes a program (or program;label) as a function and returns the value it EXITs/RETURNs; further arguments are passed to it. Exact semantics not confirmed.

XFA.doc: Extended file attribute function listed in the lexer table. It is not accepted by the 9.62 syntax checker in any tested argument form.

XOR.doc: Bitwise exclusive OR of two strings (byte by byte) or two integers (XOR(12,10)=6).
